hero.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on $95 million Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council has approved the first reading of an ordinance to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation. The land will support construction of a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange and the ongoing Midway Road widening project are designed to address a significant gap in Turnpike access and accommodate the city's growth over the next 20 to 50 years. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. City Council will vote on final approval of the land transfer at an upcoming meeting.

The Florida Department of Transportation is managing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to reduce congestion and improve safety on the roadway. The first phase is currently under construction, expanding the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction expected to begin in Summer 2027, according to the FDOT website.

In addition to widening Midway Road, FDOT is improving the Turnpike bridge and designing a partial interchange for the Turnpike. The partial interchange is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to provide additional transportation options for residents.

The construction work has not gone unnoticed by Port St. Lucie residents. Local resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged that the ongoing construction can be disruptive but believes it is necessary for the community's future. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," Scheumeister said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." Her perspective reflects the broader community recognition that while construction creates temporary inconveniences, the improvements will enhance traffic flow and accessibility throughout the city as it continues to grow.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire as electrical issue investigated
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. White's fiancé Mark discovered the fire and called friends to share the news. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who had known White for eight years, spoke about the loss and returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano, and said she was always the first to lend a hand. White was devoted to her children and loved people. Fenn noted the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his only child, Jacob, in a previous tragedy. White's birthday was scheduled for the Fourth of July, just days after her death. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes July 6 for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's public downtown dock will shut down beginning July 6 for a comprehensive renovation expected to wrap up by next Independence Day. The year-long project represents a significant investment in the city's waterfront infrastructure, with plans to substantially increase the facility's capacity. Currently accommodating 18 boat slips, the renovated dock will nearly double that number to 44 slips, serving both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The work includes construction of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and an additional smaller floating platform. A state grant and transportation impact fees are funding the project.

Beyond simply adding more space, the improvements serve a critical safety purpose for the community. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed emphasized that the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major weather events. With more than 1,400 boaters relying on the dock annually, these structural enhancements will provide greater resilience against severe storms. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, supports the improvements and expressed hope that additional floating docks might be incorporated into the final design.

The closure presents operational challenges for businesses dependent on the dock, but city officials have worked to find solutions. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger services from the dock, initially worried about continuing operations during construction. The company reached an agreement with the city to address this concern. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained that the city approved construction of a gate at the non-floating section of the dock, allowing the company to continue boarding passengers throughout the renovation period.

Kuyrkendall acknowledged the dock's existing limitations, particularly during busy weekends when space becomes tight and finding available spots grows challenging. He views the modernization project as essential for both the city and local businesses. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," Kuyrkendall said, highlighting how central the dock is to the community's identity and economic vitality. The expanded and improved dock will better serve the city's boating community while supporting the waterfront businesses that depend on convenient dock access. The project reflects Stuart's commitment to maintaining its waterfront infrastructure while preparing for future growth and storm resilience.

cards.headline: Ashley Moody and Byron Donalds unite at top of Republican ticket ahead of November general election
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Senator Ashley Moody and Congressman Byron Donalds, the leading contenders for Florida's top statewide offices, have announced a coordinated campaign strategy featuring joint appearances and mutual endorsements. The campaigns plan grassroots events designed to consolidate Republican support before the November general election. Both candidates will emphasize public safety, education, economic growth, and senior issues while contrasting their records with Democratic opponents. "Floridians deserve strong, principled leadership that puts our state first. I am proud to endorse my friend Byron Donalds," Moody said. "He is a proven conservative leader who will fight to make Florida safer, healthier, and more affordable as Governor."

Donalds reciprocated the endorsement, praising Moody's record. "Florida is fortunate to have a fighter like Sen. Ashley Moody representing Floridians," he said. "Her proven leadership as Attorney General and now as a United States Senator makes her the right choice to continue serving our state. I am proud to endorse Sen. Ashley Moody for re-election to the United States Senate." The Naples congressman entered the governor's race in early 2025 with backing from former President Donald Trump. His campaign raised $22.2 million in the first quarter, a record for a non-incumbent gubernatorial candidate in Florida, and has now accumulated over $67 million total. If elected, Donalds would become Florida's first Black governor. He faces primary competition from Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, former House Speaker Paul Renner, and businessman James Fishback. Donalds has secured endorsements from groups including the Florida Farm Bureau's FarmPAC and multiple legislative leaders.

Moody, a fifth-generation Floridian and former federal prosecutor, previously served six years as attorney general, during which she secured billions in opioid settlements for the state. Governor Ron DeSantis appointed her to the U.S. Senate seat vacated when Marco Rubio became Secretary of State. She was sworn in on January 21, 2025, and received Trump's endorsement. Moody has qualified for the special election to complete the remaining two years of Rubio's term.

The Democratic field remains in flux. Former Republican Congressman David Jolly leads the gubernatorial field with former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate. The Democratic Senate race remains unsettled following teacher Josh Weil's withdrawal due to a medical issue. The primary election is scheduled for Tuesday, August 18, with voter registration closing on July 20. The general election follows on Tuesday, November 3, with registration closing on October 5.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slips
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down on July 6 for a major $3 million renovation expected to wrap up by next Fourth of July. The project will significantly expand the dock's capacity, increasing the number of boat slips from 18 to 44 to accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funding for the renovation comes from a state grant and transportation impact fees. The completed project will feature a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform.

According to Stuart Mayor Sean Reed, the upgrades serve a critical purpose beyond simply adding more space. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. The improvements are needed given that more than 1,400 boaters rely on the dock annually. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who operates out of Stuart, supports the improvements. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said.

The city has made efforts to minimize disruption to businesses and boaters during the year-long closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger boarding services from the dock, initially worried about continuing operations during construction. However, the city found a solution by allowing the business to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained the arrangement: "So they're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here."

Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance to Stuart's identity and local businesses. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," he said. He also noted that current space constraints create challenges, especially during busy weekends when businesses struggle to find available docking spots. Kuyrkendall views the expansion positively, saying "Modernizing and expanding this back dock is really going to be great for the city but also for us as well." The renovation represents a significant investment in infrastructure that will benefit both the boating community and the broader economy that depends on waterfront access.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County to consider elevated autonomous transit network between West Palm Beach and airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
A California-based autonomous transit company called Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would carry small autonomous electric vehicles with four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Glydways said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. Gettinger referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions with estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile and argued Glydways would come in far below that range. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. The County Commission will meet Tuesday to determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin deeper discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing, with a planning and design contract potentially awarded later this year.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield for a breast reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, despite having recently undergone a double bilateral mastectomy.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alician Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says "this product is giving my patients the least amount of complications." Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem said it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with treatment standards, adding that without FDA approval, the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy." Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Zoning Commission recommends denial of controversial data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend denial of Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

A central issue during the hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Resident Laura Cole voiced concerns about the low-frequency hum generated by large-scale data centers, saying it penetrates glass and concrete. County commissioners will consider both the planning staff's recommendation for approval and the Planning and Zoning Board's recommendation for denial on July 15.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach to consider elevated self-driving transit system connecting downtown to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to the airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its elevated self-driving vehicle proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the downtown-to-airport trip to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger described the concept as a "horizontal elevator" that carries passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. The company also plans to price the service at transit-level rates rather than private rideshare prices. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners approve moving forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center delayed 3 months and $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road, said his project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced a three-month delay and approximately $90,000 in costs after contractor problems derailed his April opening. Even though the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect that included double payments to electricians, HVAC workers, and drywall contractors. The estimate does not account for lost revenue during delays or the expense of hiring another contractor to fix the problems.

Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, the organization Molen worked with, is warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Founder David Allan estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County face major issues with unvetted contractors. He recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in the county involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen's Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening on July 17.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community rallies to help fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a fire that broke out inside her Hobe Sound home Monday. The sheriff's office's preliminary findings point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief, describing it as "a terrible shame and awful loss of life." She reflected on White's character, saying she was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, having lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as White's birthday was July 4th and she passed just days before. "She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV steps in
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, turned to WPTV for help with a roofing contractor he said left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 and said he was mostly satisfied with the work, except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. After the company stopped responding to his emails and visits to their building, McCoy said he had no luck getting repairs completed despite contacting them multiple times between January 10 and February 5.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing had not paid for materials supplied to McCoy's property. Worried about legal costs and potential court proceedings, McCoy reached out to WPTV for help. After investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke directly with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, the situation quickly resolved. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien from his property. The contractor also agreed to send crews back to fix the two problem areas on his roof, completing the work about an hour after McCoy received the waiver.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football aims for state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with a clear objective: winning a state championship. Last season, the team finished with a 10-2 record and captured the district title, but their playoff run ended in disappointment during the second round. That early exit has motivated the program to pursue bigger goals this year.

The Scots are banking on continuity and experience to help them reach new heights. Head coach Jimmy Robertson noted that most of the team's seniors are four-year players who came through the middle school program, giving them deep familiarity with how the program operates. Robertson expressed confidence that the senior class has already experienced significant success during their time with the team and that their final year could represent the best season in program history. With these veteran leaders in place, the Scots believe they have the foundation to make a deeper postseason run.

To compete at a higher level, Saint Andrew's deliberately scheduled more challenging opponents for the 2026 season. Senior Jack Williams explained that the program wanted to elevate itself by testing themselves against stronger teams, which also helps attract new talent to the program. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that success for this team comes down to one measure: playoff advancement. While going undefeated in the regular season would be nice, Whelche said an undefeated record means nothing if the team keeps losing in the second round of the playoffs. The focus remains on progressing further in the postseason tournament.

The team is using summer workouts as fuel for their championship aspirations. The daily grind of training serves as a constant reminder of what they are working toward. Senior Edmyer St. Jean noted that the accumulation of hard work each day gives the team something to look forward to, with the hope that this extra effort translates into improved results when the season begins. By breaking their current record and advancing past their second-round plateau, the Scots believe they can accomplish their ultimate goal of a state title run.

cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many belongings.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely while praising the swift response by Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city, accommodating growth that has already occurred and growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike, both still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, though she ultimately received the surgery with help from her plastic surgeon.
cards.body:
Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Clark completed the mastectomy but less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh used in breast reconstruction that is popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment.

Dr. Alician Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week later, thanks to Billington. Anthem responded to the denial by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with latest treatment standards, but noted that without FDA approval, the mesh does not meet standards required for their medical policy coverage.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation

The situation escalated when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien on McCoy's home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing failed to pay for materials furnished to his property. WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing and spoke with the owner. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized. The contractor also committed to sending crews back to fix the two problem areas on the roof. About an hour after McCoy received the waiver, crews were back on his roof finishing the job.

cards.headline: Golf training center near Delray Beach delayed three months and costs $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach, says contractor problems delayed the opening by three months and cost $90,000 in repairs.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced significant delays and costs after contractor problems. The project was delayed three months from its scheduled April opening after the licensed contractor hired to prepare the space failed to complete work properly. Molen said the work ultimately had to be redone, creating what he described as a costly domino effect. He estimated the issues cost him $90,000, not including revenue lost during the delays or the expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. Despite the setbacks, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening on July 17.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates July 4 with fireworks, pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse will host a full day of free community activities, live entertainment and fireworks on July 4.
hero.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar.

Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. The center's offerings include guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Ashley Moody and Byron Donalds unite at top of Republican ticket ahead of November general election
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Senator Ashley Moody and Congressman Byron Donalds, the leading contenders for Florida's top statewide offices, have announced a coordinated campaign strategy featuring joint appearances and mutual endorsements. The campaigns plan grassroots events designed to consolidate Republican support before the November general election. Both candidates will emphasize public safety, education, economic growth, and senior issues while contrasting their records with Democratic opponents. "Floridians deserve strong, principled leadership that puts our state first. I am proud to endorse my friend Byron Donalds," Moody said. "He is a proven conservative leader who will fight to make Florida safer, healthier, and more affordable as Governor."

Donalds reciprocated the endorsement, praising Moody's record. "Florida is fortunate to have a fighter like Sen. Ashley Moody representing Floridians," he said. "Her proven leadership as Attorney General and now as a United States Senator makes her the right choice to continue serving our state. I am proud to endorse Sen. Ashley Moody for re-election to the United States Senate." The Naples congressman entered the governor's race in early 2025 with backing from former President Donald Trump. His campaign raised $22.2 million in the first quarter, a record for a non-incumbent gubernatorial candidate in Florida, and has now accumulated over $67 million total. If elected, Donalds would become Florida's first Black governor. He faces primary competition from Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, former House Speaker Paul Renner, and businessman James Fishback. Donalds has secured endorsements from groups including the Florida Farm Bureau's FarmPAC and multiple legislative leaders.

Moody, a fifth-generation Floridian and former federal prosecutor, previously served six years as attorney general, during which she secured billions in opioid settlements for the state. Governor Ron DeSantis appointed her to the U.S. Senate seat vacated when Marco Rubio became Secretary of State. She was sworn in on January 21, 2025, and received Trump's endorsement. Moody has qualified for the special election to complete the remaining two years of Rubio's term.

The Democratic field remains in flux. Former Republican Congressman David Jolly leads the gubernatorial field with former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate. The Democratic Senate race remains unsettled following teacher Josh Weil's withdrawal due to a medical issue. The primary election is scheduled for Tuesday, August 18, with voter registration closing on July 20. The general election follows on Tuesday, November 3, with registration closing on October 5.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds secures endorsement from Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson, completing Cabinet sweep
cards.teaser: The Naples congressman now has backing from Florida's entire Cabinet and both incoming legislative leaders in the Republican gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson endorsed Byron Donalds for governor, joining Attorney General James Uthmeier and CFO Blaise Ingoglia in backing the Naples congressman. The three Cabinet incumbents represent Florida's full slate of statewide elected officials. Simpson, who has led the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services since 2023, said Donalds is a trusted conservative who stands with farmers, ranchers, and rural communities and will protect land and water resources while ensuring Florida families have access to fresh, healthy food.

Simpson's Friday endorsement follows support this week from Uthmeier, Ingoglia, Senate President-designate Jim Boyd, and House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison. Donalds called Simpson a strong voice for agriculture, rural interests, and conservative values. The campaign announced Wednesday it has crossed $90 million in total fundraising, including $23 million raised in the second quarter. Donalds carries endorsements from President Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., House Speaker Mike Johnson, U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ted Cruz, 17 of 19 U.S. House Republicans from Florida, more than 75% of Florida House Republicans, nine Florida Senate Republicans, and a majority of Florida sheriffs. Polling has consistently shown Donalds with double-digit leads over GOP contenders including Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, investor James Fishback, and former House Speaker Paul Renner.

cards.headline: Florida breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company denied coverage for reconstruction surgery involving GalaFlex mesh less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, citing the treatment as investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure involving GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh. According to the denial letter, the surgery is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body and popular among plastic surgeons, it is not approved specifically for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the mesh's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and photojournalist Matthew Apthorp, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield stated it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that without FDA approval, the mesh does not meet their coverage standards. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago.

cards.headline: Tampa hosts Liberty by the Bay as Hillsborough County marks America's 250th birthday with countywide celebrations
cards.teaser: Tampa's flagship America250 celebration at Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park will feature a 250-drone light show and fireworks, with festivities planned across Hillsborough County.
cards.body:
Tampa will host Liberty by the Bay at Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park from 4 to 9:30 p.m. on July 4 as Hillsborough County marks America's 250th birthday. The free event features a Kids Zone, food trucks, beer garden, live music, DJ entertainment, a patriotic pet show, water ski show, and Kids Liberty Procession. A 250-drone light show and fireworks finale are scheduled from 9 to 9:30 p.m. The celebration extends along the Tampa Riverwalk with the Friends of the Riverwalk Patriotic Boat Parade from 6:15 to 8 p.m., the Armature Works Fourth of July event, and Freedom Fest aboard the American Victory Ship beginning at 6 p.m.

Communities across Hillsborough County are hosting Independence Day celebrations. Temple Terrace will hold its 51st annual Fourth of July celebration with a morning parade at 10 a.m. near the Family Recreation Complex and evening festivities at Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club with fireworks around 9:15 p.m. Plant City will host its annual Fourth of July Celebration at Plant City Stadium from 5 to 9:30 p.m. with live music, food trucks, vendors, family activities, and fireworks at 9:15 p.m. Lutz will start early with races at 7:30 a.m., a one-mile fun run at 8:15 a.m., and a parade at 9 a.m. starting at Lutz Lake Fern Road and Crooked Lane. Organizers advise attendees to plan ahead for parking, traffic, heat, and possible weather delays.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg Pier and Clearwater lead Pinellas County America250 Fourth of July celebrations
cards.teaser: The St. Pete Pier's sixth annual The Fourth celebration will double the scale of fireworks in honor of America's 250th anniversary, while Clearwater hosts a two-day festival at Coachman Park.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg and Clearwater are leading Fourth of July celebrations across Pinellas County as communities mark America's 250th birthday. St. Petersburg will host its sixth annual "The Fourth" Independence Day Celebration at the St. Pete Pier from 4 to 10 p.m. on July 4, featuring live music, a craft beer garden, Uncle Sam's Market, a family fun zone, food vendors and roaming entertainment. Organizers indicate this year's fireworks at 9 p.m. will "double in scale and splendor" in honor of America's 250th anniversary. The Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital Pier Run offers a four-mile run or walk along the St. Pete Pier and downtown waterfront beginning at 6:15 a.m.

Clearwater is hosting an expanded two-day celebration at Coachman Park on July 3 and 4, featuring a children's zone, musical performances, street performers, a military and veteran appreciation tent, a silent disco and food vendors. The July 3 program includes a laser light show with an FX finale at 9:15 p.m., while the July 4 event includes a patriotic fireworks display at 9:15 p.m. BayCare Ballpark will celebrate with Clearwater Threshers games and the team's largest postgame fireworks display after each game. Additional celebrations throughout the county include Dunedin's Hometown USA at TD Ballpark beginning at 6 p.m. July 3 with fireworks around 9:30 p.m., St. Pete Beach's Red, White and BBQ at Horan Park from 5 to 9 p.m., and Gulfport's events beginning at 9 a.m. at City Hall with fireworks from Williams Pier at 9 p.m.

cards.headline: Fort Lauderdale and Broward cities host America250 parades and drone shows for Fourth of July
cards.teaser: Fort Lauderdale's Fourth of July Spectacular features country singer Walker Hayes and a new drone show, while Pembroke Pines, Sunrise, and Coral Springs expand their Independence Day offerings.
cards.body:
Across Broward County, cities are rolling out free parades, concerts, drone shows and fireworks to mark the nation's 250th birthday. The event includes a kids' zone with inflatable water slides and face painting, beach games, contests and live bands throughout the afternoon. Country singer Walker Hayes will perform at 7:30 p.m., followed by a drone show at 8:45 p.m. and a fireworks display over the Atlantic Ocean. Expect heavy traffic and street closures along A1A and Las Olas Boulevard.

In Sunrise, the Stars and Stripes: 250 Years of Smiles Parade starts at 9 a.m., followed by family activities at City Park with a splash pad, fun zone and snow cones. Evening festivities resume at 6 p.m. outside Amerant Bank Arena with live music from the Higher Ground Band, food vendors, a drone show and fireworks. Coral Springs hosts its Fourth of July Celebration at Mullins Park from 4 to 9:30 p.m., featuring food vendors, sports zones, inflatables, arts and crafts, and live music from The Introverts and Absolute Bon Jonvi, a Bon Jovi tribute band. Fireworks are scheduled for 8:45 p.m. Lauderdale-by-the-Sea's Independence Day Parade begins at 10 a.m. from Town Hall, followed by Family Fun Day at El Prado Park from 11 a.m. and fireworks at 9 p.m. Broward Parks and Recreation is waiving entrance fees at regional parks on July 4.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach hosts Fourth on Flagler with new laser show for America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: West Palm Beach's Fourth on Flagler will feature a new Florida Crystals laser show synchronized with an 18-minute fireworks display, billed as the largest free outdoor Independence Day event in South Florida.
cards.body:
West Palm Beach will host Fourth on Flagler from 5 to 10 p.m. on July 4 along Flagler Drive from Banyan Boulevard to Fern Street on the West Palm Beach Waterfront. The city bills the celebration as the largest free outdoor Independence Day event in South Florida. The event features live entertainment across three stages, a patriotic flag ceremony, a kids interactive zone, and food and beverage vendors. For the first time, the city is adding a Florida Crystals laser show, timed to an 18-minute fireworks display over the Intracoastal Waterway.

Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration stretches from 5 to 9:30 p.m. along East Atlantic Avenue, between the Intracoastal Bridge and A1A. Festivities begin with the opening of a 1976 bicentennial time capsule at 5 p.m., followed by a 60-foot flag-raising at 6 p.m. and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society. The evening includes food trucks, children's activities, and live entertainment highlighted by an Earth, Wind & Fire tribute band, with fireworks at 9 p.m.

hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slips
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down on July 6 for a major $3 million renovation expected to wrap up by next Fourth of July. The project will significantly expand the dock's capacity, increasing the number of boat slips from 18 to 44 to accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funding for the renovation comes from a state grant and transportation impact fees. The completed project will feature a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform.

According to Stuart Mayor Sean Reed, the upgrades serve a critical purpose beyond simply adding more space. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. The improvements are needed given that more than 1,400 boaters rely on the dock annually. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who operates out of Stuart, supports the improvements. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said.

The city has made efforts to minimize disruption to businesses and boaters during the year-long closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger boarding services from the dock, initially worried about continuing operations during construction. However, the city found a solution by allowing the business to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained the arrangement: "So they're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here."

cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Resident Laura Cole voiced concerns about noise generated by large-scale data centers, saying low-frequency hum penetrates glass and concrete. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners.
